Picodash

Active graph: packages/panel + apps/web + apps/lab.

Current architecture baseline: `@picodash/store` provides typed state/validation foundations;
`@picodash/panel` provides rendering, registry, layout, and control surfaces.

Project status: public preview; Issues are available for feedback, and pull requests are currently disabled.

Package import surface:
- picodash
- @picodash/panel/advanced
- @picodash/panel/dashlet
- @picodash/panel/ui
- @picodash/panel/style.css
- @picodash/store

What it provides:
- application-owned panel stores via createPicodashPanelStore
- PicodashProvider, PicodashPanel, PicodashItem, built-in inputs and charts
- centralized shadcn aria-rhea primitives via @picodash/panel/ui
- third-party dashlets can compose the same first-party Button, Card, Input, Select, Slider, Tabs,
  overlay, and form primitives; every public primitive has a named *Props type
  and the structural shell components in `@picodash/panel/dashlet`.
- use component variant/size props and semantic --picodash-* tokens; raw implementation variant
  helpers and internal component paths are not part of the public UI contract
- public visualization tokens include --picodash-color-well, --picodash-color-data-1,
  --picodash-color-data-2, --picodash-color-data-3, --picodash-color-data-4, and
  --picodash-color-data-5
- provider-scoped panel visibility, activation, reactive placement, and runtime setPlacement via usePicodashPanel
- typed store behavior and strict contracts from @picodash/store (fields, setFieldValue(s), validate/parse,
  repair proposals).
- floating, fixed, and hybrid placement modes with free, snapped, and docked dispositions; snaps
  stay offset and floating-like, while Hybrid side/corner targets use an animated proxy and dock
  fixed-like on release; docked Hybrid panels resist detachment and remain Hybrid after becoming free
- viewport-default geometry with provider panelBoundary and per-panel boundary Element/ref overrides
- unified body collapse for free/snapped panels and whole-panel retraction for docked panels,
  with pinned start/end lanes and a scroll-faded auto lane in fixed-like layouts
- explicit application-owned reads via usePicodashPanelStoreSelector(store, selector)
- advanced provider access via usePicodashProviderSelector and usePicodashProviderStoreApi
- contextual advanced panel access via usePicodashPanelSelector and usePicodashPanelStoreApi
- optional panel close buttons with hide or deregister behavior
- action-menu API is public/composable on `PicodashPanel`:
  - `actionMenu` undefined => default menu
  - `actionMenu = false` => no action menu
  - `actionMenu` as `readonly ReactElement[]` => root submenu with default trigger
  - `actionMenu` as `ActionSubmenu` => replaces root submenu trigger
- Public exports include `ActionMenuItem`, `ActionSubmenu`, `ActionMenuSeparator`,
  `CopySubmenu`, `ExportSubmenu`, `CopyJsonItem`, `CopyYamlItem`, `ExportJsonItem`,
  `ExportYamlItem`, `ExpandAllItem`, `CollapseAllItem`, `ImportItem`, `ResetItem`.
- `destructive` tuple: `[message, title?, buttonLabel?]`, with default `title = label` and
  `buttonLabel = 'Confirm'`.
- strict programmatic writes, sync validation, JSON-compatible values
- pointer and keyboard item reordering with same-band constraints
- observable async sparkline source failures
- complete package dark/light themes, system color-scheme resolution, and CSS custom themes via `data-picodash-theme`
- strict custom provider theme unions through `PicodashProvider<CustomTheme>`
- provider-root and optional panel-level theme scopes, with inherited primitives and portal-root carriers
- lazy Recharts and react-dropzone implementations behind stable public components
- import/export and repair flows

Production pages (`apps/web`):
- /, /store, /usage, /usage/components, /more-examples, /themes, /docs

Local debugging pages (`apps/lab`, not deployed with the production website):
- / and /lab redirect to /lab/state
- /lab/state/provider, /lab/state/scene, /lab/state/built-in-items, /lab/state/custom-items
- /lab/panel-geometry, /lab/panel-interaction, /lab/dashlets

`/demo` and the former debugging routes hosted by `apps/web` are not active production routes.

App surface mapping:
- apps/web: production Next.js website
- apps/lab: local-only Next.js debugging app

Important migration:
- The old schema-driven registration API and persistence formats are retired; map old `panel` specifiers to `@picodash/panel` imports.
- Only canonical Picodash layout records hydrate; invalid or obsolete records start from declared defaults.
- No compatibility facade is provided.
- Gearmo is a known breaking consumer requiring separate migration planning.
- Typed field-handle integration in built-ins and compound dashlets is still migrating; track state in `docs/internal/e2e-migration-ledger.md`.

Ports:
- 6030 web development server via WEBSITE_PORT
- 6031 web production preview (start) server via WEBSITE_PORT
- 6032 local lab development server via LAB_PORT
- 6033 web E2E server via WEBSITE_PORT
- 6034-6039 can be temporarily allocated to worktrees for non-conflicting development and E2E servers
- if an allocated port is occupied, agents should find a free port in 6034-6039 for brief server runs
- `bun run port:reserve` claims the lowest available worktree port and writes both WEBSITE_PORT and LAB_PORT to the worktree `.env.local`
- `bun run port:release` removes the current worktree reservation after its PR is merged

Verification:
- bun install --global vercel before using the deployment scripts
- bun run lint
- bun run format
- bun run --filter @picodash/web lint
- bun run --filter @picodash/web format
- bun run --filter @picodash/panel lint
- bun run --filter @picodash/panel format
- vp run @picodash/panel#build before workspace-wide checks or builds
- bun audit --audit-level=high
- bun run --cwd packages/panel release:check
- bun run ready
- bun run web
- bun run lab
- bun run port:reserve
- bun run port:release
- bun run deploy
- bun run deploy:prod
- bun run --filter @picodash/lab lint
- bun run --filter @picodash/lab format
- bun run --filter @picodash/lab check
- bun run --filter @picodash/lab build
- bun run --filter @picodash/web check
- bun run --filter @picodash/web test:e2e
- apps/web/tests/routes.spec.ts asserts the production route boundary and local lab route markers
- GitHub CI runs parallel quality and E2E jobs for pull requests and main pushes
